extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: SciQ is a dataset of 13,679 crowdsourced multiple choice science exam questions covering topics in biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics. Each question has 4 answer options (one correct) and most instances come with a supporting document used to formulate the question. The dataset has a multiple choice version and a direct answer version (where systems must predict the answer span within a passage).
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. In the first step, crowd workers are shown three filtered in-domain textbook paragraphs and asked to formulate a question-answer pair based on one of them (or reject all). In the second step, a different worker validates the (question, answer) pair and selects or writes three distractors, aided by model-generated distractor suggestions from a random forest ranker trained on real science exam questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 science study textbooks from online learning resources including CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science and physics at elementary through college introductory level, shared under Creative Commons License. Also used 3,705 real 4th and 8th grade science exam questions (80% train/20% validation) to train the distractor ranking model.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to paragraphs from the base corpus of science textbooks. Sentences were filtered out based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatic, and complexity rules (e.g., removing questions/exclamations, sentences without verb phrases, with modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstrative pronouns, non-third-person pronouns, first names, fewer than 6 or more than 18 tokens, more than 2 commas, special characters, references to graphs/tables/links, discourse markers, absolute wording, or instructional vocabulary). A paragraph was accepted if a minimum number of its sentences were accepted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-step annotation: (1) Question Formulation Task: workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs and asked to pick one and write a question-answer pair following guidelines (no yes/no questions, no need for further context, query general principles, question length 6-30 words, answer length up to 3 words, no ambiguity, clear from paragraph). Workers could reject all three paragraphs. (2) Distractor Selection Task: workers saw a (q, a) pair plus six model-suggested distractors, first judged whether the question could appear in a school science exam (92.8% pass rate), then selected up to two suggested distractors and wrote at least one original distractor.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Crowd workers accepted model-predicted distractors about half of the time; 36.1% of the distractors in the final dataset were generated by the model. Qualitative evaluation showed humans could identify real exam questions vs SciQ questions in only 55% of cases, below significance level p=0.05.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with Master's status participated in the crowdsourcing project. No further demographic information provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Random forest classifier (scikit-learn implementation, 500 trees, minimum 4 samples per leaf) for distractor candidate ranking, using features including GloVe embeddings, POS-tag consistency, singular/plural consistency, word frequency, Levenshtein edit distance, suffix consistency, token overlap, numerical content indicators, units of measure, WordNet hypernymy indicators, and OpenIE-based knowledge base links.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions and answers are relatively short. A small percentage of passages from unreleasable texts meant the direct-answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller (10,481 train, 887 dev, 884 test) than the multiple choice version (13,679 total). The dataset is restricted to science domain (biology, chemistry, earth science, physics) at elementary to introductory college level.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing data for science exam question answering, reading comprehension models in medium-data settings, and as augmentation training data to improve performance on real 4th and 8th grade science exam questions. Two versions: multiple choice (without passage) and direct answer (with passage). Dataset split: training (~11,679), validation (1,000), test (1,000) for multiple choice version.
